The development is seen as a significant step towards regulating the use of artificial intelligence and data analytics in pricing decisions. According to reports, the ban will prevent companies from using personal data to charge different prices to different customers for the same product or service.

The use of personal data, such as browsing history and location, to determine prices can result in some customers being charged higher prices than others for the same product or service. This has raised concerns about the potential for price gouging and exploitation of vulnerable consumers. The ban on surveillance pricing is seen as a way to promote fairness and transparency in pricing practices, and to protect consumers from unfair treatment.

The bill passed by New York lawmakers specifically prohibits the use of personal data to set prices, except in cases where the customer has explicitly opted in to such practices. Despite these concerns, the ban is seen as a significant step towards promoting fairness and transparency in pricing practices, and is expected to have a positive impact on consumers.

The ban on surveillance pricing in New York is part of a broader trend towards regulating the use of artificial intelligence and data analytics in business practices. Other states, including California and Nevada, have already implemented similar bans, and there are efforts at the federal level to introduce national regulations on the use of personal data in pricing decisions. The move is seen as a response to growing concerns about the potential risks and consequences of using personal data in business practices, and is expected to have significant implications for companies operating in the US.

The passage of the bill in New York is expected to pave the way for similar legislation in other states, and may ultimately lead to a national ban on surveillance pricing. As the use of artificial intelligence and data analytics continues to grow, lawmakers and regulators are likely to face increasing pressure to regulate these practices and protect consumers from potential harm.
